task.title: Execute an explicit workflow-phase provider turn
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/743 by composing one caller-selected phase through the existing tool-free assistant authority boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Deliver only selected phase skills to the provider in deterministic exact-ID order.
Exclude unrelated registrations and fail malformed or missing bindings before transcript or provider side effects.
Persist successful human and assistant turns durably.
Do not mutate workflow lifecycle or grant tools.

attempts.diagnostic: The runtime had explicit composed turns but no method accepting and resolving a workflow phase.
attempts.patch: Added provider-order, unrelated-skill, missing-binding, malformed-binding, terminal-phase, and side-effect tests.

attempts.summary: Composed phase resolution with the existing turn path.
attempts.diagnostic: Resolving before transcript persistence and then reusing composed tool-free completion preserved fail-closed ordering and existing authority semantics.

attempts.summary: Strengthened durable success evidence during review.
attempts.diagnostic: The original test asserted the returned session but did not independently prove storage-backed replay.
attempts.patch: Reloaded the session from SessionStore and asserted both persisted turns before merge.

outcome.summary: A caller-selected phase can influence one tool-free provider turn through explicit registered skills, without becoming workflow execution or lifecycle authority.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-kernel --test workflow_phase_runtime --test composed_skill_runtime

lessons: Resolve caller-selected phase bindings before any transcript or provider side effect.
Provider prompt authority can reuse existing explicit composition without coupling workflow lifecycle.
Storage-backed reload assertions distinguish durable behavior from returned in-memory state.
